# Results — Study 861 (Debt-Maturity Rollover Risk)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **firms
funded with a high share of SHORT-TERM debt carry rollover risk and subsequently UNDER-earn,
especially when rates rise / credit tightens (2022+).** Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Prices fingerprint `6067630c220d`
(yfinance daily adjusted closes); events cache = 1,732 (ticker, filing) rows.*

Stamped as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `6067630c220d`

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **32** large, debt-carrying US filers that tag a clean maturity split on EDGAR (of a 48-name basket; the rest report only one debt leg and carry no rollover-share signal — fixed, current survivors) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: `DebtCurrent`, `LongTermDebtCurrent`, `LongTermDebtNoncurrent` (anchored on the noncurrent leg's 10-Q/10-K filing date; a missing short-term leg is a genuine zero); de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **1,732** debt quarters, period ends **2008-07-31 → 2026-05-03**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `st_share` = (DebtCurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent) ÷ (DebtCurrent + LongTermDebtCurrent + LongTermDebtNoncurrent) — the fraction of total debt maturing within a year |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, **long the LOW-share (safe) tercile / short the HIGH-share (rollover-risk) tercile**, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Direction | the claim predicts the low-minus-high portfolio is **positive** (risky firms under-earn); a *negative* significant result would be the WRONG sign (a risk premium) and stamp `NONE` |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** The monthly cross-section averages ≈26 names but is thinner in
2008-09; only 32 of the 48 basket names tag `DebtCurrent`/`LongTermDebtCurrent`/`LongTermDebt`​`Noncurrent`
cleanly enough to form the share, so this is not the whole large-cap universe. **No survivorship
correction:** the basket is current survivors — it cannot contain the firms whose rollover wall
actually sank them (the exact left tail the story is about), which biases a long-low/short-high
claim portfolio **conservatively**. Named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (do high-rollover-risk firms under-earn?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short (long low-share / short high-share) on `st_share`, one
execution lag, 2009-08 → 2026-06 (**203 months**, avg cross-section 26.2 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **+46.7 bps/month** (+5.61%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | **+2.65** |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+3.22** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | 0.64 |
| monthly hit rate | 59% |
| long (low-share) / short (high-share) leg | +143.1 / +96.4 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×2.42 over 203 months |

The high-short-term-share (rollover-risk) names **under-earn the safe, termed-out names by ≈47
bps/month**, and the spread clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar on the autocorrelation-robust statistic
(**NW *t* = +3.22**, one-sample +2.65). It is right-signed — exactly the claimed penalty. A
staleness-200 variant is materially the same (+41.1 bps, NW *t* = +2.69), and the balance-sheet-
**scaled** signal `(DebtCurrent+LongTermDebtCurrent)/Assets` agrees: +34.1 bps/month, **NW *t* =
+2.67**.

### Robustness — it is not one name and not one spec

| cut | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| primary (terciles, staleness 400) | **+3.22** |
| drop-one-name jackknife (32 refits) | **all > +2.0** (min +2.14 dropping OKE, max +3.72 dropping GILD) |
| halves / quartiles / quintiles | +3.87 / +2.69 / +2.27 |
| staleness 200 days | +2.69 |
| asset-scaled `(ST debt)/Assets` | +2.67 |

Every specification clears the bar, and no single name carries it.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by signal, 1-day-lag entry)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `st_share`; low-minus-high forward drift, entered one day
after the filing:

| horizon | n | high-share (top) | low-share (bottom) | long-short (low−high) | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 1,730 | +0.86% | +1.34% | **+0.48%** | +1.29 | 52% | 0.105 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 1,710 | +2.96% | +4.26% | **+1.30%** | +2.02 | 53% | 0.018 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 1,686 | +6.02% | +8.85% | **+2.83%** | +2.85 | 52% | 0.000 |

The drift builds with horizon and clears |t| = 2 at a quarter and beyond, with a label-shuffle
placebo *p* of 0.018 / 0.000 — a random tercile split beats the real one essentially never at 3-6
months. The tercile means (63 d, low→high: +4.26% / +2.42% / +2.96%) are **not a clean monotone
ladder** — the effect is really the **low-share (safe) tercile out-earning** the rest, not a
smooth penalty across the whole distribution. But the extremes are correctly ordered and the
event study agrees with the calendar long-short: high-rollover-risk names under-earn.

## Era cut at 2022 — the penalty bites harder when rates rise

Calendar long-short, split at 2022-01-01 (the Fed hiking cycle — the claim's specific prediction):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2009-2021 (low/falling rates) | 149 | +32.6 bps | +2.10 |
| 2022-2026 (hiking / tight credit) | 54 | **+85.7 bps** | **+2.95** |

The under-earning of high-short-term-share firms is present in both regimes but **~2.6× larger in
the rising-rate sub-period** — precisely the "rollover risk bites when rates rise" mechanism the
claim names. (Alternate splits agree: the post-2017 half is +62 bps NW *t* +2.83; the post-2019
half +65 bps NW *t* +2.51.)

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted penalty (high-`st_share` names drift
down, low-share names up); no network. Detector = the primary claim long-short (long low / short
high) NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **−0.41** (sd 1.33), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **2/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 861) | **+7.13** (mean +226.5 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (two borderline crossings in twelve HAC *t*'s, ~as expected
by chance) and lights up hard on a planted penalty. The real-tape NW *t* = +3.22 is therefore a
genuine effect, not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of a real-tape stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.10 — a slow quarterly balance-sheet signal):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | +40.5 bps/mo | +4.86%/yr | **+2.79** | 0.56 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | +34.3 bps/mo | +4.11%/yr | **+2.36** | 0.47 |
| 30 bps | 200 bps | +23.9 bps/mo | +2.86%/yr | +1.64 | 0.33 |
| 50 bps | 300 bps | +11.4 bps/mo | +1.37%/yr | +0.78 | 0.16 |

The gross edge **survives realistic costs** (still NW *t* = +2.36, Sharpe 0.47 at 20 bps + 100 bps
borrow) — the turnover is low, so friction only trims ~1.5%/yr. But it is a **modest** net Sharpe
and it **breaks under a harsher cost/borrow assumption** (NW *t* falls to +1.64 at 30 bps + 200 bps
and +0.78 at 50 bps + 300 bps). Survives the base case, dies under stress: that is `FRAGILE`, not
a robust `INVESTABLE`.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The low-minus-high short-term-share long-short is **right-signed and
  robustly significant**: +46.7 bps/mo, one-sample *t* = +2.65, **Newey-West *t* = +3.22**; it
  holds across the 2022 era split (both halves NW *t* > 2, and larger post-2022 exactly as the
  claim predicts), survives a 32-name drop-one jackknife (every refit NW *t* > 2), and is
  confirmed by the pooled event drift (63 d *t* = +2.02, 126 d *t* = +2.85, placebo *p* ≤ 0.02).
  High-rollover-risk firms under-earn — the claim is confirmed on this tape.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Net of 20 bps + 100 bps borrow the edge survives (NW *t* = +2.36,
  Sharpe 0.47, +4.1%/yr), but the net Sharpe is modest and the significance breaks under a
  harsher 30 bps + 200 bps assumption (NW *t* = +1.64). A real edge on the base cost model that
  is one cost-bump from vanishing.
- **Rate-era prediction — CONFIRMED.** The under-earning is ~2.6× larger in the 2022+ rising-rate
  sub-period (+85.7 bps, NW *t* = +2.95) than before (+32.6 bps, NW *t* = +2.10). Rollover risk
  does bite harder when rates rise.

**Honest reading.** This is a genuine positive — rare on the desk — but note *what* it is: much
of the spread is the **safe, termed-out mega-cap leg out-earning**, so it may partly ride a
quality / low-volatility / defensive tilt rather than pure rollover causation, and the survivor
basket omits the firms the rollover wall actually killed (which would only strengthen a
long-low/short-high). Real signal, fragile-but-present tradability, and a mechanism that behaves
exactly as the rates story says.
